slides.narration: Welcome to Book II, Chapter 20: Working with Files, Paths, Time, and Randomness. This deck follows the Chapter 1 Slides model: concept on the left, code or evidence on the right, and presenter notes that tell the instructor what to say and do. Modern C++ is not about using the newest syntax because it looks impressive. It is about encoding ownership, lifetime, invariants, generic behavior, and failure boundaries so the program is easier to reason about and harder to misuse.

slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 20, treat 20.1.2 Reading and Writing Binary Files as a design decision with costs and evidence. Binary mode controls platform text transformations; it does not make an in-memory object representation into a portable format. The example writes four explicit eight-bit octets on the documented platform baseline and reconstructs a 32-bit value by shifts in a chosen big-endian order. Do not serialize a struct by dumping sizeof(struct) bytes when portability or confidentiality matters. Padding, endianness, type widths, and representation can differ, and padding can contain unintended data. A wire format should specify field widths, byte order, versioning, and validation independently of the compiler’s object layout. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 20, treat 20.2.1 Inspecting Files and Directories as a design decision with costs and evidence. Filesystem queries can inspect existence, type, size, or directory entries. Many facilities offer throwing and error-code forms. Choose an error-handling policy deliberately and avoid treating a failed query as equivalent to an absent file. A check followed by a later operation can race with another actor changing the filesystem. For example, checking that a path is safe and then opening it does not create an atomic security boundary. This chapter’s isolated test directory avoids that shared-adversary scenario; secure production file handling requires platform-appropriate techniques and threat modeling. keyPoints: The application calculates the correct report but fails while writing it.

slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 20, treat Failure clinic — A successful computation with failed publication as a design decision with costs and evidence. The application calculates the correct report but fails while writing it. Returning success because the calculation completed misreports the externally visible operation. Check the output state and define an exit status for publication failure. At the same time, do not claim that an error status erased bytes already written to a terminal, pipe, or file. Detection and rollback are different properties. A second failure assumes that a successful existence check proves a later open will succeed. A third reads a structure directly from disk and discovers that padding or byte order differs on another build. A fourth expects a fixed dice sequence from every library because the engine seed is fixed. Each defect arises from promoting a narrow observation into a stronger guarantee that the interface did not supply. A graduate-level explanation should say what the abstraction buys, what rule keeps it honest, and what artifact proves the rule: source code, compiler acceptance or rejection, stdout, stderr, exit status, object state, or a test witness.
